reuse_rationale: Apache License 2.0 is a permissive open source license that allows commercial use, modification, distribution, and sublicensing. The license requires preservation of copyright notices and disclaimers but does not impose copyleft requirements. The code can be freely integrated into proprietary or open source UML-Codex project with proper attribution. REGnosys has made this available as part of FINOS (Fintech Open Source Foundation) promoting industry collaboration.

components.name: rune-lang
components.description: Core language module containing Xtext grammar (Rosetta.xtext), AST definitions, parser, type system, validation, scoping, and code generators. Built on Eclipse Modeling Framework (EMF) and Xtext.
components.value_proposition: Complete reference implementation of a financial domain DSL showing grammar design, type system implementation, validation framework, and multi-target code generation

components.name: rune-runtime
components.description: Runtime library providing base classes and interfaces for generated code including RosettaModelObject, builders, metadata support, and label providers
components.value_proposition: Shows runtime architecture needed to support generated DSL code, including immutable data patterns, builder patterns, and metadata handling

components.name: rune-ide
components.description: IDE integration module providing Eclipse/VSCode support through Language Server Protocol (LSP), syntax highlighting, code completion, validation, and navigation
components.value_proposition: Complete IDE integration showing LSP implementation for DSL tooling support

components.name: rune-maven-plugin
components.description: Maven plugin for DSL code generation and formatting during build process
components.value_proposition: Shows build tool integration patterns for DSL compilation and code generation workflows

components.name: rune-testing
components.description: Testing utilities for DSL validation, compiler testing, and model validation
components.value_proposition: Testing infrastructure for DSL implementations including test models and validation utilities

components.name: rune-integration-tests
components.description: Integration test suite for end-to-end DSL functionality testing
components.value_proposition: Integration testing patterns for DSL projects

components.name: rune-tools
components.description: Utility tools for DSL development and analysis
components.value_proposition: Supporting tools for DSL development workflow

design_patterns.description: Uses Eclipse Xtext framework to define language grammar in declarative .xtext format. Grammar automatically generates parser, lexer, AST, and basic editor support
design_patterns.implementation: Rosetta.xtext defines complete grammar with imports from three Xcore models (Rosetta.xcore, RosettaSimple.xcore, RosettaExpression.xcore)
design_patterns.benefit: Rapid language development with automatic tooling generation
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - UML-Codex could leverage Xtext for grammar definition and automatic parser generation

design_patterns.description: Uses Eclipse Modeling Framework (EMF) Ecore for metamodel definition. Xcore provides extended syntax for defining metamodels with behavior
design_patterns.implementation: Three Xcore models define the metamodel structure, referenced by the Xtext grammar
design_patterns.benefit: Strong typing, model validation, serialization, and code generation from metamodel
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - EMF is standard for UML tools and provides rich metamodeling capabilities

design_patterns.description: MWE2 (Modeling Workflow Engine) orchestrates multi-stage generation: grammar to parser, metamodel to Java classes, models to target code
design_patterns.implementation: GenerateRosetta.mwe2 defines workflow with XtextGenerator, parser fragments, scoping, serialization, and custom optimization fragments
design_patterns.benefit: Separation of concerns in generation pipeline, extensible through custom fragments
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: APPLICABLE - UML-Codex needs multi-stage generation for different output targets

design_patterns.description: Comprehensive type system with 29 type-related classes supporting parametrized types, generics, enums, choices, data types, and type inference
design_patterns.implementation: TypeSystem.java coordinates RType hierarchy including RDataType, REnumType, RChoiceType, RParametrizedType, with TypeFactory for instantiation
design_patterns.benefit: Rich type checking, inference, and validation capabilities
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - UML requires sophisticated type system for classes, interfaces, generics, etc.

design_patterns.description: Validation framework using visitor pattern with specialized validators for each construct type (attributes, choices, enums, functions, types, reports)
design_patterns.implementation: RosettaValidator coordinates AttributeValidator, ChoiceValidator, EnumValidator, FunctionValidator, TypeValidator, ReportValidator
design_patterns.benefit: Modular, extensible validation with clear separation of concerns
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - UML needs extensive validation of constraints, multiplicities, and well-formedness rules

design_patterns.description: Custom scoping mechanism for resolving references across namespace boundaries with import support
design_patterns.implementation: RosettaScopeProvider with AliasAwareImportNormalizer, PatchedImportNormalizer, RosettaLinkingService, RosettaQualifiedNameProvider
design_patterns.benefit: Proper namespace isolation and cross-reference resolution
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - UML has complex package structure and qualified name resolution requirements

design_patterns.description: Interpreter pattern with typed value objects (RosettaBooleanValue, RosettaNumberValue, RosettaStringValue, etc.) for expression evaluation
design_patterns.implementation: RosettaInterpreter with RosettaValueFactory creating strongly-typed value objects with context management
design_patterns.benefit: Type-safe runtime evaluation of DSL expressions
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: APPLICABLE - Useful for evaluating OCL constraints and UML expressions

design_patterns.description: Abstract representation of target languages enabling multi-language code generation
design_patterns.implementation: TargetLanguageRepresentation and TargetLanguageStringConcatenation provide language-agnostic code generation with Java as default implementation
design_patterns.benefit: Single DSL can generate code in multiple programming languages
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - UML-Codex needs to generate code in multiple languages (Java, Python, C++, etc.)

design_patterns.description: Generated code produces immutable model objects with nested builder classes for construction
design_patterns.implementation: All generated types implement RosettaModelObject, are immutable after creation, and include nested Builder implementing RosettaModelObjectBuilder
design_patterns.benefit: Thread-safe, predictable objects with fluent construction API
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: APPLICABLE - Good pattern for generated model classes from UML

design_patterns.description: Rich metadata system with annotations for scheme, key, reference, template, location, address, and custom qualifiers
design_patterns.implementation: Annotation syntax in grammar with metadata attachment to types and attributes
design_patterns.benefit: Extensible metadata without changing core metamodel
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: APPLICABLE - UML has stereotypes and tagged values serving similar purpose

design_patterns.description: Declarative mapping from external formats (FpML, ISDACreate) to internal model through synonym annotations
design_patterns.implementation: Synonym sources with path expressions, conditional mappings (set when, set to), and merge strategies
design_patterns.benefit: Separation of data transformation logic from core model
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: MODERATELY_APPLICABLE - Could be used for mapping between different UML profiles or serialization formats

design_patterns.description: Linking model elements to regulatory documents through hierarchical reference system (body, corpus, segment)
design_patterns.implementation: Document references attached to model elements with publisher, document set, and section identifiers
design_patterns.benefit: Traceability to requirements and regulatory sources
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: APPLICABLE - Similar to requirements traceability in UML models

design_patterns.description: Separates function API specification from implementation, allowing partial definitions requiring implementor extensions
design_patterns.implementation: Functions can be fully defined, partially defined, or purely specified. Output construction uses 'set' and 'add' keywords with alias support
design_patterns.benefit: Supports both complete automation and human-in-the-loop approaches
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - UML operations can be abstract or have method bodies

design_patterns.description: First-class cardinality constraints on all attributes with (min..max) syntax, supporting optional, required, and collections
design_patterns.implementation: RCardinality type with CardinalityProvider for computation, integrated into type system
design_patterns.benefit: Clear data integrity rules enforced at model and runtime levels
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - Direct mapping to UML multiplicities

design_patterns.description: Explicit choice types representing mutually exclusive attribute sets (similar to union types or XSD choice)
design_patterns.implementation: Choice type with required-choice, optional-choice, and one-of conditions enforced through ChoiceValidator
design_patterns.benefit: Type-safe representation of alternatives without inheritance
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: MODERATELY_APPLICABLE - UML doesn't have direct choice construct but pattern useful for specific domains

design_patterns.description: Embedded expression language with functional operations: filter, map (extract), reduce (sum/min/max), sort, flatten, distinct
design_patterns.implementation: Rich expression hierarchy in grammar supporting path expressions, operators, conditionals, and collection transformations
design_patterns.benefit: Powerful declarative query and transformation capabilities
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: HIGHLY_APPLICABLE - Similar to OCL (Object Constraint Language) in UML

design_patterns.description: Deliberately limits language expressiveness to prevent infinite loops and complex control flow, making it accessible to domain experts
design_patterns.implementation: No while loops, no goto, limited recursion - only if-then-else, switch, and functional list operations
design_patterns.benefit: Guaranteed termination and easier formal verification
design_patterns.applicability_to_uml: APPLICABLE - UML Action Language and OCL have similar constraints

notes:
The REGnosys rune-dsl repository is a sophisticated domain-specific language implementation for financial regulatory compliance modeling. Despite being named 'rune-dsl', the internal implementation consistently uses 'Rosetta' naming, which is the actual DSL name. This is a fork of the FINOS (Fintech Open Source Foundation) project.

Key architectural decisions:
1. Built on Eclipse Modeling Framework (EMF) and Xtext - industry standard for DSL development
2. Multi-module Maven project with clear separation: lang, runtime, IDE, testing, tools, maven-plugin
3. Grammar-driven development with automatic parser and tooling generation
4. Rich type system (29 classes) supporting parametrized types, generics, enums, choices
5. Multi-target code generation with Java as default target
6. Language Server Protocol (LSP) integration for modern IDE support
7. Embedded expression language with functional programming features (filter, map, reduce)
8. Deliberately Turing-incomplete to ensure termination and accessibility to domain experts

The DSL addresses a real-world problem: siloed IT systems in financial infrastructure implementing the same regulatory processes differently. Rune/Rosetta provides a unified, human-readable representation accessible to non-programmers.

For UML-Codex, this repository offers exceptional value:
- HIGHLY_APPLICABLE patterns: Xtext grammar development, EMF metamodeling, type system design, validation framework, multi-target generation, expression language, cardinality constraints
- APPLICABLE patterns: Interpreter implementation, IDE integration, build tool integration, metadata annotations
- MODERATELY_APPLICABLE: Choice types, synonym mapping, document references

Recommendations by component:
- STUDY: rune-lang (grammar and architecture), rune-ide (LSP integration), rune-integration-tests
- ADAPT: rune-runtime (patterns for generated code), rune-maven-plugin (build integration), rune-testing
- AVOID: rosetta-backport (legacy compatibility complexity)

Critical lessons:
1. EMF/Xtext is proven technology for DSL development - don't reinvent the wheel
2. Multi-stage code generation pipeline is essential for complex transformations
3. Comprehensive type system is crucial for enterprise-grade DSL
4. Modular validation framework scales better than monolithic validators
5. IDE integration via LSP is expected by modern developers
6. Build tool integration (Maven/Gradle) is essential for adoption
7. Clear separation of specification from implementation enables flexibility
8. Immutable generated code with builders is good practice
9. Documentation and examples are critical - this project falls short
10. Naming consistency matters - rune vs rosetta confusion is problematic

Dependencies are primarily Apache 2.0 (Xtext, EMF, Commons, Jackson) or EPL (Eclipse components), all compatible with commercial use.

The codebase is 85.2% Java, 14.6% Xtend (JVM language for template-heavy code), with minimal Python/TypeScript. This suggests Xtend is useful for code generation templates.

Overall assessment: This is a production-quality, enterprise-grade DSL implementation that demonstrates best practices in language engineering. While complex, it provides an excellent reference architecture for UML-Codex. The Apache 2.0 license allows code reuse with attribution. Primary concerns are complexity and documentation gaps, but the architectural patterns and design decisions are sound and directly applicable to UML tool development.
